screening_results.reason: Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal (attend vs reappraise) in human alcohol-dependent patients and matched healthy controls, and presents task-related brain activation results; no exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal (downregulation, upregulation, passive viewing) in human participants and reports task-related brain activation differences by genotype; no exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract reports a task using real-time fMRI (with simultaneous EEG) where participants learned volitional downregulation of amygdala BOLD via neurofeedback, leading to reduced amygdala reactivity to visual stimuli and improved implicit emotion regulation. These findings indicate task-related fMRI activation during an emotion-regulation task. Unclear whether regulation was performed specifically during stimulus presentation, so full-text review is recommended.

Abstract indicates an fMRI study in psychiatric patients linking stigma resistance with emotion regulation, but does not state a task-based emotion-regulation paradigm or report task-related activation results. Insufficient information to confirm I1, I2, and I4 from the abstract, so include for full-text review.

Task-based fMRI with human participants performing an emotion regulation task (automatic inhibition priming) and reporting task-related neural activation differences; abstract provides sufficient information to meet inclusion criteria for full-text review.

This is a task-based fMRI motor study of sequential finger movements, not an emotion-regulation task. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related activation). Inclusion not met: I2 (no emotion regulation/reappraisal). No exclusion criteria apply.

Empirical tDCS+fMRI study in a clinical (MDD) human sample addressing emotion-regulation regions, but the abstract does not specify a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation paradigm, stimuli, or task-related activation results. I3 is met; I1, I2, and I4 are not demonstrated in the abstract. Include for full-text review to determine eligibility.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study using cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation) in human participants (young and older adults) and reports task-related brain activation (dorsolateral prefrontal cortex). No exclusion criteria are met from the abstract.

Task-based fMRI study where human participants used cognitive reappraisal to down-regulate responses to negative pictures; reports task-related neural activation and behavioral effects. Meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are evident from the abstract.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study in humans that examined deliberate modification of emotional responses to negative stimuli (emotion regulation) in PTSD and trauma-exposed controls, and reports neural mechanisms—meeting I1-I4. No exclusion criteria apply.

Study uses resting-state fMRI rather than a task-based paradigm and does not involve participants performing an emotion regulation task or report task-related activation results. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation).

The study is a task-based fMRI experiment using cognitive reappraisal to up- and down-regulate emotions during the Ultimatum Game, reports task-related brain activations, and involves human participants. No exclusion criteria apply.

fMRI study directly comparing cognitive reappraisal and expressive suppression in human participants, examining neural bases — satisfies I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task: reappraisal and suppression), and I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Human sample is implied, so I3 is met. No exclusion criteria (E1, E2) apply.

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none (I3 not demonstrated in abstract). Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study comparing cognitive reappraisal and placebo emotion regulation, reports neural activation changes (amygdala, insula, PFC, subgenual cingulate), and involves human participants performing emotion regulation. Meets inclusion criteria I1–I4, and no exclusion criteria are evident. Include for full-text review to confirm details.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study of human participants using voluntary suppression of negative affect (an emotion regulation strategy) and examining neural substrates, reporting task-related brain activation results. This meets I1–I4 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

Inclusion met: I2 (cognitive reappraisal emotion regulation task), I3 (healthy human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation via EEG/sLORETA). Exclusion criteria: none met.

Abstract describes an original task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation) in human participants and reports task-related amygdala–prefrontal functional connectivity predicting affect attenuation. All inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Task-based fMRI study using an antecedent-focused, extrinsic/incidental reappraisal strategy (precedent descriptions) in human participants; reports modulation of amygdala and insula responses (task-related brain activation). No exclusion criteria met based on abstract. Full text recommended for extraction of details.

Meets all inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI with reappraisal and acceptance emotion-regulation tasks in human participants (rMDD and controls), and reports task-related brain activation contrasts. No exclusion criteria evident from abstract.

Task-based fMRI comparing mindfulness and cognitive reappraisal during cued expectation and perception of negative images in healthy participants; reports task-related brain activation (medial PFC, amygdala, insula, caudate). All inclusion criteria I1–I4 are clearly met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal applied to anticipatory anxiety in human participants; reports task-related brain activation and correlations with subjective anxiety. Meets inclusion criteria I1-I4; no exclusion criteria apparent from abstract.

Does not address review objective of regulating emotional responses to visual stimuli: task uses recall of autobiographical memories (non-visual). No exclusion criteria met. Task-based fMRI study in humans using a cognitive reappraisal emotion-regulation task; reports task-related brain activation (amygdala, insula, temporal, parahippocampal regions). No exclusion criteria met.

Task-based fMRI study of emotion regulation (reappraisal) reporting lower prefrontal activation, so I1, I2 and I4 are met. Abstract indicates human UHR participants but does not clearly state a separate control group for the clinical sample, so I3 is not demonstrated; include for full-text review to confirm.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal (distancing) in healthy human participants (N=76) and presents task-related brain activation/deactivation results (prefrontal cortex, amygdala). No exclusion criteria apply. Full-text review recommended to extract details.

Task-based fMRI study in human participants using cognitive reappraisal (an emotion regulation task) that reports task-related neural activation results and comparisons. No exclusion criteria apparent. Abstract satisfies inclusion criteria I1, I2, I3, and I4.

Study is a task-based fMRI investigation of cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation) in human clinical (GAD, PD) and healthy control groups and reports brain activation results. No exclusion criteria are met based on the abstract.

No task-based fMRI or task activation reported: study used resting-state fMRI correlating trait ERQ scores with amygdala connectivity. Exclusion IDs met: none. Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study in humans using an emotion regulation (reappraisal/maintain/suppress) task, includes clinical (cocaine+Cluster B) and control groups, and reports task-related brain activation and connectivity results. Task-based fMRI study using cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation) with human participants across ages; reports task-related brain activation (prefrontal, amygdala) and connectivity. No exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study of female adolescents with conduct disorder performing effortful emotion regulation and reports dorsolateral prefrontal activation differences (task-related activation). Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study in which human participants performed cognitive reappraisal of angry faces (an emotion regulation task) and reports task-related brain activation and connectivity findings. No exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation) using negative facial stimuli in healthy adult humans and reports task-related brain activation results (PFC, amygdala), meeting inclusion criteria; no exclusion criteria met.

Task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation), reports task-related activation and effective connectivity related to reappraisal success in humans; meets inclusion criteria I1-I4, no exclusions evident.

The abstract describes an empirical task-based fMRI study where 70 youth performed a cognitive reappraisal emotion-regulation task during fMRI and reports task-related neural activation/variability results related to age and affect. Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study of human young adults performing cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation) with task-related activation contrasts and results reported; does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full-text review appropriate to extract detailed activation data.

Task-based fMRI study examining voluntary attentional regulation of emotion (an emotion regulation strategy) and emotion recognition in depressed patients and controls; reports activation and connectivity results. Task-based fMRI study using cognitive reappraisal to down-regulate negative emotions; human participants including an anxiety-prone group and healthy controls; reports task-related BOLD activation contrasts during regulation versus maintain. Meets inclusion criteria I1–I4 and no exclusion criteria are evident from the abstract.

This is a task-based fMRI study (3T) with human participants performing an emotion regulation task (cognitive reappraisal) comprising 18 panic disorder patients and 18 healthy controls, and it reports task-related neural activation results and HRV. All inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Abstract reports an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy men and women using emotion regulation (cognitive reappraisal and distraction) and presents task-related brain activation results; no exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study in humans using emotion regulation strategies (reappraisal and distraction) with remitted depressed patients and healthy controls, and reports task-related brain activation (amygdala, ACC, OFC). Meets inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are indicated.

Therefore it does not meet I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (participants performing an emotion regulation task), nor I4 (reports task-related activation). It does meet I3 (human clinical and control groups). No exclusion criteria (E1/E2) apply.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study of emotion regulation (self-distraction/thought suppression) in an anticipatory anxiety paradigm, reporting neural activation results in humans. No exclusion criteria are met.

Task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal of aversive visual stimuli in human participants; reports task-related brain activation (amygdala, LPFC) and between-group comparison with/without neurofeedback. Meets all inclusion criteria; no exclusion criteria evident.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study in human participants examining cognitive reappraisal (instructed and spontaneous) and reports amygdala and prefrontal activation, so it meets inclusion criteria I1–I4. No exclusion criteria are met.

Meets inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI (I1); participants performed instructed emotion regulation using reappraisal (I2); human clinical sample (spider phobics) with clear participant group (I3); reports task-related brain activation results (I4). No exclusion criteria apply from abstract. Recommend full-text review to extract coordinates and contrasts.

Task-based fMRI study of emotion regulation in typically developing children and adult comparison; participants performed an emotion-regulation task during frustrating episodes and authors report task-related activation and effective connectivity (ACC–amygdala). Meets I1–I4. No exclusion criteria apparent from abstract.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal in human participants with remitted MDD and controls, and reports neural (frontolimbic) mechanisms—meeting core inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Task-based fMRI study in human participants using cognitive reappraisal to up- and down-regulate socially driven emotions during a Dictator Game, and reports task-related brain activation results. This meets I1-I4 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (no non-empirical paper; participants were instructed to regulate their emotions).

Task-based fMRI in human participants directly comparing multiple emotion regulation strategies (detachment, reinterpretation, distraction, expressive suppression) during downregulation of negative emotions; reports task-related brain activation (prefrontal, amygdala) fitting the meta-analysis objective. Task-based fMRI study in human participants directly comparing reappraisal and distraction as emotion regulation strategies; reports subjective emotion ratings and task-related brain activation and functional connectivity (e.g., amygdala, prefrontal, parietal regions). Meets inclusion criteria for task-based fMRI, emotion regulation task, participant sample, and brain activation results.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study of voluntary emotion regulation that reduces amygdala activation to aversive stimuli, indicating human participants performed an emotion regulation task and task-related brain activation was reported. No exclusion criteria are met from the abstract.

Task-based fMRI study examining neural correlates of two emotion regulation strategies (reappraisal and distraction) in healthy human participants at high risk for bipolar disorder; reports task-related brain activation. No exclusion criteria met based on abstract.

Task-based fMRI in humans manipulating implicit cognitive reappraisal (preceding descriptions) fits the emotion regulation definition; reports task-related activation (prefrontal, amygdala) in 25 participants. No exclusion criteria met. Abstract provides sufficient evidence that I1–I4 are satisfied.

Task-based fMRI study examining cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation) in human participants; reports task-related activation and pattern-information results linked to regulation success. Meets inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are met based on the abstract.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study using an emotion-regulation task (cognitive reappraisal), with human participants (excess-weight and normal-weight controls), and reports task-related activation and connectivity results. No exclusion criteria are met based on the abstract.

Meets all inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI (I1) with emotion regulation tasks (reappraisal and distraction) during presentation of emotional images (I2); human participants including BD patients, unaffected relatives, and matched controls (I3); reports task-related brain activation and connectivity results (I4). No exclusion criteria met.

Task-based fMRI study in children/adolescents instructed to up- and down-regulate responses to disgusting images (cognitive reappraisal). Reports task-related brain activation and age-related effects. No exclusion criteria met.

Include for full-text review to determine imaging modality and task details.

Task-based fMRI in human participants using a short mindfulness emotion regulation intervention during anticipation and perception of negative pictures; reports task-related brain activations (prefrontal, amygdala, insula). Satisfies I1-I4; no exclusion criteria met.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study of cognitive emotion regulation in previously depressed and healthy children, reporting neural activation differences during regulation. Meets inclusion criteria I1, I2, I3, and I4; no exclusion criteria evident.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study using a cognitive reappraisal emotion-regulation paradigm in human participants (regular marijuana users and matched controls) and reports task-related brain activation results (amygdala, prefrontal networks). No exclusion criteria appear to apply.

Task-based fMRI comparing two emotion regulation strategies (distraction and reappraisal) reporting decreases in negative affect and region-specific activation changes (amygdala, prefrontal, cingulate). Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study using emotion regulation (reappraisal) in human participants and reports task-related activation (dorsolateral/ventrolateral PFC, cingulate). All inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Task-based fMRI study using cognitive reappraisal to regulate negative emotions and reporting neuronal correlates in borderline patients. Abstract does not clearly state whether a separate control group is reported, so full text needed to confirm I3. Include for full-text review.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study (N=58) where participants performed cognitive reappraisal of negative and neutral visual stimuli and reports specific brain activations (DLPFC, lateral OFC). This satisfies I1-I4 and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

Meets all inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI of human participants performing cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation), includes adolescent/young adult sample, and reports task-related brain activation results (amygdala and PFC). No exclusion criteria met.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion met: I3 (human adolescent sample). Inclusion NOT met/demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (participants performing an emotion regulation task during scanning), I4 (task-related brain activation results). Study reports structural MRI and questionnaires only.

Meets all inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI of emotion regulation (cognitive reappraisal and distraction), healthy human participants, and reports task-related BOLD activation results. No exclusion criteria are met.

Adult human participants performed a cognitive reappraisal emotion-regulation task during task-based fMRI; task-related activation results are reported (vmPFC, extrastriate cortex); study includes a patient (obesity) and separate healthy control group. No exclusion criteria met.

Task-based fMRI using visual negative-emotion pictures with induced heat pain to probe pain-mediated affect regulation; includes clinical (BPD) and control groups; reports task-related neural results (amygdala activation/deactivation and connectivity). Task-based fMRI study of emotion regulation comparing reappraisal and acceptance in healthy adults; reports task-related BOLD activation and behavioral/autonomic outcomes. Abstract satisfies I1, I2, I3, and I4 with no exclusion criteria met.

Abstract suggests neural circuit changes related to emotion regulation linked to sleep, but does not specify task-based fMRI methods, the use of an explicit emotion-regulation task, or task-related activation results. Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study with human participants viewing emotion-evoking visual stimuli and reports task-related brain activation differences between groups; meets inclusion criteria for task-based emotion regulation or viewing and reports activations. No exclusion criteria met.

Task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal in human participants (ages 15–25) reporting task-related brain activation (amygdala, fusiform, temporal-occipital). Meets all inclusion criteria; no exclusion criteria apply.

No task-based fMRI or task-related activation reported: the study used resting-state fMRI and measured spontaneous (trait) reappraisal. Inclusion met: I3 (human participants). Task-based fMRI study with human participants instructed to use Compassion-meditation and Reappraisal to modulate emotional responses to film clips, and reports task-related brain activation. Thus meets I1,I2,I3,I4. No exclusion criteria are met from the abstract.

Task-based fMRI pilot in children explicitly testing cognitive reappraisal (an emotion-regulation strategy) and reporting brain responses and self-reported affect, meeting inclusion criteria I1–I4. No exclusion criteria met.

Task-based fMRI with human participants using emotion-regulation strategies (cognitive reappraisal and expressive suppression), including proactive/anticipation regulation; reports task-related brain activation results. No exclusion criteria met in the abstract.

Task-based fMRI study in healthy human participants viewing emotional visual stimuli; examines habitual emotion regulation (expressive suppression), including anticipatory/antecedent processes, and reports task-related brain activation. Task-based fMRI study in human participants examining emotion regulation (implicit attention shift and appraisal) and reporting task-related brain activations; no exclusion criteria met in the abstract.

Task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal (up- and down-regulation) using visual stimuli (angry faces) in patients with depression and healthy controls; reports task-related neural activation (amygdala, insula, prefrontal regions). No exclusion criteria met.

Task-based fMRI study of human participants performing cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation). Abstract reports task-related brain activation results (amygdala, prefrontal) during regulation. No exclusion criteria met.

Abstract reports comparisons of gambling disorder patients and healthy controls using brain activation measures of emotion regulation, indicating a task-based fMRI investigation of emotion regulation in human participants. Include for full-text review to confirm task specifics and contrasts.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study of human participants performing emotion regulation of negative visual stimuli, examining SSRI effects and 5-HTTLPR moderation and reporting neural (fMRI) outcomes. Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation) in adolescent girls with PTSD and reports task-related amygdala functional connectivity changes associated with symptom reduction. Abstract describes an empirical task-based rtfMRI neurofeedback study in healthy human participants targeting hippocampal activation to enhance emotion regulation. Exclusion criteria are not met. Abstract indicates an fMRI task involving observation of risk-taking actions and suggests investigation of emotion-related processing; it is unclear whether participants actively regulated emotions or merely viewed stimuli. Title and abstract indicate a task-based fMRI study of emotion regulation in adolescent major depressive disorder, reporting amygdala response and functional connectivity consistent with task-related brain activation. Study reports task-based fMRI in human participants performing cognitive reappraisal (watch vs reappraise) with clinical (SAD) and healthy control groups, and reports task-related brain activation/connectivity results. No exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study in which human participants cognitively up-regulated (engaged) positive-social emotions from a first-person perspective and reports fMRI activation and effective connectivity results. Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation) during peer-rejection in depressed and non-depressed adolescents and reports functional connectivity/brain activation findings. Task-based fMRI with healthy human participants instructed to regulate (expressive suppression) and imitate emotional facial expressions while viewing dynamic visual stimuli; reports task-related brain activation. Meets I1–I4. No exclusion criteria met.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation) in healthy human participants, with voxelwise task-related brain activation results (PFC and amygdala). This satisfies inclusion criteria I1–I4 and no exclusion criteria are met based on the abstract.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study in smokers using cognitive reappraisal to regulate craving (emotion regulation). Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study of human participants performing explicit emotion regulation (up-/downregulation) while viewing negative images, reports task-related brain activation (VLPFC, amygdala), and includes clinical groups and healthy controls. No exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study with human participants performing an active cognitive emotion regulation task (cognitive reappraisal), includes both depressed patients and healthy controls, and reports whole-brain activation and connectivity results relevant to regulation vs. passive viewing; meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are met.

Meets all inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI of human participants performing cognitive reappraisal (down-/up-regulation) of visual/episodic negative images, reports task-related brain activation results. No exclusion criteria met.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study in humans using a cognitive reappraisal emotion-regulation task, reports task-related brain activation and connectivity results, and includes healthy adult participants. All inclusion criteria are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study in adult humans using instructed cognitive reappraisal (Social-Reg) versus look, reporting task-related brain activation contrasts and associations with behavior; meets inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are evident.

Task-based fMRI with human participants instructed to regulate responses to visual food stimuli using cognitive reappraisal, suppression and up-/down-regulation; reports task-related brain activation results. No emotion regulation instruction reported (I2 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (task-related brain activation results). Task-based fMRI in human participants comparing emotion-regulation-related instructions (permit/accept vs view) during viewing of unpleasant and neutral visual stimuli; reports subjective ratings and task-related brain activation (amygdala). Meets I1–I4 and no exclusion criteria apply.

Task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal in adult human participants that reports task-related brain activation (PFC and amygdala). The abstract meets inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are apparent, so include for full-text review.

Abstract reports neural activity during explicit emotion regulation in humans and links it to resting-state vmHRV, implying a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation study that reports task-related brain activation. Meets inclusion criteria I1-I4; no exclusion criteria met.

Meets inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI of cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation) in human participants (children/adolescents with ASD and TD controls) and reports task-related brain activation and connectivity results. No exclusion criteria met.

Task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation) in human participants; reports task-related brain activation (prefrontal, cingulate, occipital, subcortical) across experiments, meeting inclusion criteria for meta-analysis.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation) using standardized negative scripts in human participants, with clinical and control groups and task-related brain activation results. This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that directly tests emotion regulation (reappraisal and suppression) while viewing negative pictures and reports neural activation results, satisfying the review objective and inclusion criteria.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study using cognitive reappraisal (distancing) in healthy human participants and presents task-related brain activation results (ventral striatum, fronto-parietal network). No exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract reports an empirical task-based fMRI study of an emotion regulation (ER) task in human participants (n=60) and presents task-related neural activation changes pre- to post-training. No exclusion criteria are met.

Task-based fMRI with human participants (N=10) performing emotion regulation tasks (reappraisal and affect labeling) and reporting task-related brain activation (amygdala, IFG). Tasks involve regulating emotional responses and fit the meta-analysis objective. No exclusion criteria met.

Abstract reports cognitive reappraisal of palatable food images in human participants across a BMI range and describes modulation of neural responsivity—matching emotion regulation of visual stimuli and task-related brain activation. Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study in which SAD patients performed emotion-regulation tasks (breath-focused and distraction-focused attention) while reacting to negative self-beliefs and shows task-related brain activation changes (amygdala and attentional regions). Include for full-text review to confirm visual-stimuli requirement and presence/absence of separate control group.

Task-based model-based fMRI in human participants using cognitive emotion regulation (aversive conditioning with and without regulation), reporting prediction error-related and task-related neural activation. No exclusion criteria met.

Human task-based rtfMRI study reporting task-related activation and voluntary modulation of emotional states via neurofeedback. Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study using a film-based emotion regulation task in human adolescents/young adults and presents task-related neural activation results (prefrontal cortex, amygdala). No exclusion criteria are met.

Task-based fMRI study of emotion regulation (reappraisal/detachment) with passive viewing; includes clinical (AN) and age-matched control groups; reports behavioral arousal ratings and task-related fMRI activation results—meets all inclusion criteria.

Task-based real-time fMRI neurofeedback study in human adolescents (7–16) teaching up-/down-regulation of an emotion-regulation region (insula); reports task-related activation and connectivity. Abstract reports a randomized, placebo-controlled task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation) in healthy adults and presents task-related activation and functional connectivity results (amygdala and dlPFC). Study reports a task-based fMRI experiment in healthy human (female) participants performing voluntary emotion regulation of emotional pictures and reports task-related brain activation results; matches I1, I2, I3, and I4. No exclusion criteria met.

Patient-only fMRI neurofeedback study (Patients n=10) with no separately reported control group in the abstract. Inclusion criterion not met/not demonstrated: I3 (no control group reported for the patient sample). Exclusion criteria: none met (E1,E2 not applicable).

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study including an explicit cognitive emotion regulation task and an emotional Stroop, includes patient and control groups, and reports task-related brain activation (left supramarginal gyrus). No exclusion criteria met. Include for full-text review.

Task-based fMRI study (N=26) of primiparous mothers using distraction to regulate emotions in response to infant crying; reports reduced amygdala activation with regulation. Satisfies I1,I2,I3,I4. Excluded because the study uses resting-state fMRI acquired before and after an emotion-regulation task rather than reporting task-based fMRI activation; therefore I1 (task-based fMRI) and I4 (task-related activation results) are not met. Abstract reports a neuroanatomical MRI study of somatoform disorders with no mention of task-based fMRI, emotion regulation tasks, or task-related activation results. Task-based fMRI in humans comparing emotion regulation strategies (cognitive reappraisal and expressive suppression) to natural viewing of visual scenes; reports task-related brain activation results and manipulates stimulus valence and social content. Excluded because the study did not use task-based fMRI (I1 not met); it used magnetoencephalography and structural MRI. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (task involving inhibition of aversive socio-emotional stimuli), I3 (human participants—school-age children), I4 (reports task-related functional brain activity). Exclusion criteria met: none.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study (I1) using cognitive emotion regulation/reappraisal during reward anticipation (I2) in healthy human participants (I3) and reports task-related brain activation results (DLPFC, putamen, PPI) (I4). No exclusion criteria are met; include for full-text review.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study in human participants (38 males) and reports task-related neural responses in emotion-regulation networks during virtual violent actions. Meets all inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI (I1); participants performed an implicit emotion regulation task (I2); includes clinical SAD group and healthy controls reported separately (I3); reports task-related brain activation/connectivity results (PPI amygdala-vmPFC) and pre/post treatment changes (I4). No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants with patient and control groups), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). This is a structural MRI/DTI study comparing gray matter volume and FA in children; it is NOT a task-based fMRI study and does not report task-related activation or any emotion regulation task. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion IDs not met: I1 (not task-based fMRI), I2 (no emotion-regulation task), I4 (no task-related brain activation results).

Abstract reports an fMRI study of older adults with amnestic MCI addressing affective regulation and frontal dysfunction, but does not specify a task-based emotion regulation paradigm or task-related activation results. Task-based fMRI with human participants (BPD patients and controls) reporting task-related brain activation/connectivity during viewing of negative vs neutral pictures with heat pain. Randomized, placebo-controlled task-based fMRI in human participants assessing distraction as an emotion regulation strategy in PTSD patients and controls; reports task-related brain activation and functional connectivity results (thalamus, striatum, amygdala). Task-based fMRI with human adults using instructed emotion regulation (increase/decrease negative responses) during a task; reports ACC activation and connectivity related to errors (task-related brain activation). Fits inclusion criteria I1-I4; no exclusion criteria met.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study where human participants used cognitive reappraisal to up- and downregulate emotional responses to visual threat-related stimuli; reports task-related brain activation (amygdala, prefrontal regions) and physiological/self-report measures. Abstract lacks key details: it does not state whether task-based fMRI was used, whether participants performed an explicit emotion regulation task, or whether task-related brain activation results are reported. Meets all inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI (I1), an implicit emotion-regulation/emotion-label task (I2), human adolescent participants (I3), and reports task-related brain activation and connectivity results (I4). No exclusion criteria met.

Task-based human fMRI study where smokers viewed emotionally evocative anti-smoking messages; reports task-related activations (amygdala, vmPFC) and a regulation-related brain pattern moderating responses. Task-based fMRI in healthy humans (n=18) using an emotion regulation task (reappraisal) and reporting task-related activations (vmPFC, amygdala). Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study in humans (12 females, 12 males) performing emotion regulation (view vs regulate emotional responses to pictures) and reports task-related brain activation results. Task-based fMRI in 40 healthy human participants viewing emotion-eliciting images while applying emotion regulation strategies (goal vs. implementation intentions). Task-based fMRI study in human participants (spider-phobic patients) using cognitive reappraisal as an emotion regulation strategy and reporting fMRI activation related to regulation; fits I1–I4. Abstract indicates a neuroimaging study of emotional cue processing but does not specify task-based fMRI, whether participants performed an emotion-regulation or passive viewing task, or report task-related activation results. Task-based fMRI study in humans reporting task-related brain activation during anticipation of emotional visual stimuli. Task-based fMRI with human participants performing an emotion regulation task (up-regulation of positive emotions to visual images), healthy sample, and reports task-related brain activation (ventral striatum). No exclusion criteria met in abstract.

Task-based fMRI study with human participants (24 women) performing cognitive reappraisal/social-distance emotion regulation; reports task-related brain activation (dmPFC, aPCC, amygdala) and peripheral measures. Meets inclusion I1–I4; no exclusion criteria met.

Task-based fMRI in healthy human participants that manipulates and reduces appetitive/emotional responses to visual food cues via an aversive aftertaste (a regulation-like cognitive control of appetite). Reports task-related brain activation. No exclusion criteria are met.

The study is a task-based fMRI study (I1), with human participants (I3), and reports task-related activations (I4), but it does not involve participants performing an emotion regulation task—it uses an emotional oddball/distraction paradigm without instructions to regulate emotional responses (I2 not met). No exclusion criteria are met (none applicable).

Task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation) in human participants (psychosis-prone vs low), reporting task-related brain activation and functional connectivity. Fits all inclusion criteria; no exclusion criteria apply.

Task-based fMRI study using emotional (angry/neutral) faces during a working-memory task with patient and control groups; reports task-related functional connectivity differences. The review objective allows studies that view emotional stimuli without explicit regulation, so include for full-text to confirm whether regulation instructions were used. Inclusion criteria met: I1, I3, I4. I2 (explicit emotion regulation) not demonstrated in abstract.

Task-based rtfMRI neurofeedback in human participants that involves voluntary self-regulation of emotional (amygdala) activity with positive emotion induction and reports task-related connectivity/activation results; meets inclusion criteria I1–I4. No exclusion criteria met from abstract.

The abstract describes a task-based (3T fMRI) study using the shifted-attention emotion appraisal task (SEAT), a test of emotional processing and regulation, in human participants given DHEA or placebo, and reports task-related brain activation and connectivity results. No exclusion criteria are met. Recommend full-text review.

Task-based fMRI with adolescent participants and task-related activation reported (I1, I3, I4). Abstract does not clearly state participants were instructed to regulate their emotional responses (I2 not demonstrated). Because it’s unclear whether the task constitutes an emotion-regulation instruction rather than measurement of emotion-related distraction, include for full-text review to determine I2.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study in human patients performing an emotion regulation task (cognitive reappraisal to down-regulate negative affect), and reports task-related brain activation results. This satisfies inclusion criteria I1–I4; no exclusion criteria are met.

Task-based fMRI study reporting task-related cortical–amygdala coupling during anticipation of a public speech (I1, I4). It examines anticipatory emotional processes relevant to emotion regulation, but the abstract does not state that participants were instructed to regulate nor whether a control group is reported, so full-text review is needed to confirm I2 and I3.

Task-based fMRI in human participants manipulating incentives to regulate emotional reactions to visual/peer stimuli; reports task-related neural activation differences for regulation of positive vs negative emotions. Fits broad definition of emotion regulation (deliberative regulation in decision-making) and meets all inclusion criteria.

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human clinical sample reported). Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I1 (no clear task-based fMRI described), I2 (no emotion-regulation task or instructions described), I4 (no task-related activation results reported). Abstract describes structural, diffusion, and functional connectivity analyses rather than an emotion-regulation or stimulus-viewing task. No exclusion criteria clearly met.

Task-based fMRI study with human clinical and control groups (Complicated Grief, Non-Complicated, Nonbereaved) reporting task-related activations. Abstract does not specify an explicit emotion-regulation instruction (ecStroop likely measures emotional processing/attentional bias rather than directed regulation), so criterion I2 is unclear from abstract alone; full-text needed to confirm whether the paradigm meets the review’s emotion-regulation definition.

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met or not demonstrated: I1 (no mention of task-based fMRI), I2 (not an emotion-regulation task for visual stimuli; focuses on pain modulation), I3 (participants/sample not clearly reported), I4 (no task-related brain activation results reported).

Task-based fMRI study in human children (ages 8–10) performing voluntary emotion regulation (reappraisal/suppression) of sad film excerpts; reports task-related brain activation loci. No exclusion criteria are met.

Task-based fMRI study in humans (patients with SAD) where participants performed emotion regulation (reappraisal) of social evaluation and the paper reports task-related brain activation changes; meets I1-I4 and no exclusion criteria are met based on the abstract.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study investigating emotion regulation in ADHD, matching the review objective. However, it does not specify whether a separate control group was reported or explicitly state task-related activation results in the abstract. Include for full-text review to confirm control group reporting and reported activation results.

Study uses Cyberball to measure neural responses to social exclusion but does not indicate participants were instructed to regulate their emotional responses. Thus it does not meet the emotion-regulation task criterion (I2).

Task-based fMRI study examining neural circuitry supporting emotion regulation using an emotional n-back task in human clinical groups; reports task-related anterior cingulate activation distinguishing bipolar vs unipolar depressed females. Inclusion criteria I1, I3, and I4 are clearly met; I2 is reasonably met because the study targets emotion regulation circuitry and uses emotional stimuli (fits the review objective of regulation or viewing). No exclusion criteria apply.

Study is a task-based fMRI with human participants instructed to maintain or regulate emotional responses to visual social stimuli (regulation task). Reports task-related brain activation analyses. No exclusion criteria met (not a review; not mere perspective-taking).

Excluded because the task is a simple motor response flexibility task rather than an emotion regulation task. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (adolescent human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion not met: I2 (does not involve regulation of emotional responses to visual stimuli). No exclusion criteria met (E1,E2).

I2 (emotion regulation task) not demonstrated: abstract describes viewing threatening stimuli and measuring reactivity but no instruction to regulate. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (healthy human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). No exclusion criteria met (E1,E2).

Task-based fMRI study in 19 healthy adults that explicitly instructs emotion regulation (cognitive reappraisal and expressive suppression) and natural attending; reports task-related brain activation. No exclusion criteria met.

Task-based fMRI study reporting cognitive emotion regulation (reappraisal) during scanning in human participants (female sample) with task-related brain activation results (amygdala and prefrontal coupling). No exclusion criteria met and all inclusion criteria are satisfied.

Abstract reports a tDCS-fMRI study aiming to modulate implicit emotion regulation in human participants but does not clearly state a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation task or report task-related activation. Key inclusion criteria (I1, I2, I4) are uncertain from abstract alone, so INCLUDE for full-text review to clarify.

Study uses resting-state fMRI rather than a task-based emotion regulation or viewing paradigm. It includes clinical (ASD) and control participants (I3 met) but does not involve an emotion regulation task (I2), is not task-based (I1), and does not report task-related activation results (I4). No exclusion criteria (E1/E2) apply.

Excluded (E2): This is a task-based fMRI study (I1) with human participants (I3) reporting task-related activations (I4), but it measures mentalizing/perspective-taking without instruction to alter participants' emotional responses—fits exclusion E2; I2 (emotion-regulation task) not met or demonstrated.

Study is a task-based fMRI with human participants and reports task-related activation (I1, I3, I4 satisfied). However, participants performed a projective storytelling/perspective-taking AAP task without instructions to regulate emotion, meeting exclusion E2. Inclusion I2 (emotion-regulation task) is not demonstrated.

Task-based fMRI investigating emotional conflict and reports fronto-limbic activity/connectivity (meets I1 and I4). Abstract does not clearly state that participants were instructed to regulate their emotional responses per inclusion definition (I2 not demonstrated) and does not specify a separately reported control group (I3 not demonstrated). Because key details are missing but the study likely fits the review, include for full-text review.

Task-based fMRI with human participants viewing religious vs nonreligious images during painful stimulation; contemplation of the religious image led to emotional detachment (an emotion-regulation-like process) and the paper reports task-related brain activations (right VLPFC). Fits inclusion criteria for emotion regulation to visual stimuli and reports brain activation results.

Study uses resting-state fMRI and examines amygdala functional connectivity in PTSD, not a task-based emotion regulation or viewing task and does not report task-related activations. Inclusion met: I3 (human clinical participants). Inclusion not met: I1, I2, I4. No exclusion criteria met.

Study used resting-state fMRI (rs-fMRI) rather than a task-based paradigm. It does not involve an emotion-regulation task with visual stimuli or report task-related activation results. It includes human clinical participants (MDD) but fails I1, I2, and I4. No exclusion criteria are met.

Study uses implicit emotional processing (gender judgment) without instructions to regulate emotion. Exclusion IDs met: []. Inclusion IDs met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human clinical and control groups), I4 (reports task-related task activation/connectivity). Inclusion IDs not met: I2 (participants performing an emotion regulation task).

Study used task-based fMRI during a psychosocial stress task and reports task-related hippocampal activation; satisfies I1, I3, I4. Abstract does not describe an emotion-regulation task (e.g., reappraisal or instructed regulation of emotional responses to visual stimuli), so I2 is not demonstrated. No exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract suggests neural investigation of regulating negative autobiographical memories but does not clearly state task-based fMRI, that participants performed an explicit emotion-regulation task, or that task-related activation results are reported. Insufficient information to confirm inclusion criteria from abstract alone; include for full-text review.

Task-based fMRI in human participants manipulating perceived control over painful stimuli as a form of cognitive reappraisal/emotion regulation; reports task-related brain activation (dACC, alPFC). Fits broad definition of reappraisal/antecedent-focused regulation. No exclusion criteria met.

Abstract reports task-based fMRI in a normative human sample and multivoxel pattern results predicting affective valence/arousal (I1, I3, I4). It does not state participants performed an emotion regulation task (I2 not demonstrated). Because inclusion is uncertain from abstract alone, include for full-text review.

Task-based fMRI in human participants using distancing (a form of cognitive reappraisal) to downregulate emotional responses to visual social stimuli; reports whole-brain task-related activation results (amygdala, PFC, precuneus, etc.). Meets inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria apparent.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study using a cognitive reappraisal strategy (core emotion-regulation approach) with reported neural activity/connectivity and refers to human participants. It does not specify regulation of emotional responses to visual stimuli explicitly, so inclusion in the visual-stimulus-specific meta-analysis is uncertain — include for full-text review.

Task-based fMRI with human participants performing an implicit emotion-regulation task (derogation of attractive alternatives). Reports task-related brain activation results (VLPFC, pDMPFC, ventral striatum). Meets inclusion criteria I1–I4; no exclusion criteria apparent from abstract.

The study is task-based fMRI with OCD and control groups and reports task-related activation (I1, I3, I4). However, the task elicits shame and guilt via imagined scenarios and does not describe any emotion-regulation instructions (reappraisal, distancing, acceptance) or viewing/regulating of visual stimuli. Inclusion criterion I2 (emotion regulation task) is not demonstrated; no exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract reports an empirical task-based fMRI study in children performing emotion regulation while viewing emotionally expressive faces and reports task-related ACC activation patterns. This meets inclusion criteria I1–I4; no exclusion criteria apply.

Longitudinal task-based fMRI where adults performed effortful emotion regulation of negative stimuli; reports task-related activation (amygdala, ventrolateral/dorsolateral PFC). Meets I1-I4; no exclusion criteria met.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study where participants (SAD patients) used an instructed emotion-regulation strategy (“reality-checking”) during anticipation and perception of emotional stimuli and reports task-related brain activation results. Inclusion criteria I1, I2, and I4 are clearly met. It is unclear from the abstract whether a separate healthy control group is reported (I3 not demonstrated), so include for full-text review to confirm.

Meets inclusion: task-based fMRI (I1); uses an emotion regulation task (cognitive reappraisal) (I2); human adolescent participants (I3); reports task-related brain activation (amygdala and prefrontal activation) (I4). No exclusion criteria met. Abstract clearly describes fMRI emotion regulation paradigm with neural results, so include for full-text review.

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human adolescent participants). Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (participants performing an emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation results). The study reports resting-state functional connectivity rather than a task-based emotion regulation paradigm, so it does not meet the meta-analysis inclusion criteria.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study in human (BPD) participants examining neural correlates of provocation-focused rumination, but does not specify that participants regulated emotional responses to visual stimuli or used standard emotion-regulation instructions (e.g., reappraisal). Eligibility for the meta-analysis is therefore uncertain from the abstract and warrants full-text review.

Excluding because the study is a task-based fMRI study with clinical and control adolescent groups and reports task-related activations (I1, I3, I4 met). However, it does not describe an emotion-regulation task or instructions to amplify/dampen emotional responses (I2 not met). No exclusion criteria (E1/E2) apply.

Task-based fMRI in human participants (N=24) instructed to view or decrease emotional responses to pictured stimuli (emotion regulation). Reports task-related brain activation. No exclusion criteria met (not a review/meta-analysis, not an empathy/perspective-taking study without regulation instruction).

Abstract reports investigation of behavioral and neural markers of emotion regulation in older adults (human participants), but does not explicitly state it used task-based fMRI, a specific emotion regulation task with visual stimuli, or report task-related activation. Insufficient information to confirm I1, I2, and I4 — include for full-text review.

Task-based rtfMRI neurofeedback study where human participants performed a sustained emotion regulation task (voluntarily modulating positive/negative states) and task-related brain activation results are reported. Meets inclusion criteria I1, I2, I3, I4; no exclusion criteria are apparent from the abstract.

Task-based fMRI study in humans where participants were instructed to up- and down-regulate emotional responses to aversive visual scenes (cognitive reappraisal strategies), and the abstract reports task-related brain activation results (prefrontal, amygdala). No exclusion criteria met.

Task-based fMRI with 20 healthy human participants viewing aversive visual stimuli and reporting task-related BOLD activation. Abstract does not describe an instructed emotion-regulation task, but the review objective includes passive viewing of emotional stimuli; thus study is eligible for full-text review.

Title/abstract indicate a task-based fMRI study in human patients (women with BPD) investigating emotional modulation of response inhibition, but the abstract does not specify whether participants performed an explicit emotion-regulation task or only viewed emotional stimuli, nor does it give task-related activation details. Insufficient information to confirm I2 and I4 from the abstract alone, so include for full-text review.

Task-based fMRI with 21 healthy human participants performing emotion regulation strategies (mindfulness and suppression) in response to emotional visual stimuli; reports task-related brain activation results (amygdala attenuation and connectivity). Satisfies all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are met.

Task-based fMRI in depressed patients performing intentional emotion-introspection to down-regulate unpleasant affect, with task-related brain activation reported (amygdala, insula, PFC). Unclear from abstract whether regulation was applied to visual stimuli, so include for full-text review to resolve this.

Meets all inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI; participants performed effortful emotion regulation (emotional faces n-back assessing voluntary attentional control); includes schizophrenia patients with matched healthy controls reported separately; reports task-related brain activation results. No exclusion criteria are evident from the abstract.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study (I1) where participants explicitly regulate emotion (reduce negative, enhance positive) reflecting CBT-like reappraisal strategies (I2), includes human clinical (medication-free MDD) and matched control groups reported separately (I3), and reports task-related brain activation results (I4). No exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract reports task-based fMRI with human participants and reports task-related brain activation (I1, I3, I4). However, there is no evidence participants performed an emotion regulation task or were instructed to regulate their emotional responses (I2 not demonstrated). No exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract reports task-based fMRI in clinical out-patients examining brain activation to emotional facial expressions (meets I1, I3, I4). It does not state whether participants were instructed to regulate their emotional responses (I2 not demonstrated). No exclusion criteria met. Abstract insufficient to determine regulation vs passive viewing; include for full-text review.

E2 met: this is an empathy/perspective-taking viewing task without instruction to regulate emotions. Inclusion met: I1, I3, I4 (task-based fMRI; human participants; reports task-related activations). Inclusion not met/not demonstrated: I2 (no evidence participants performed an emotion regulation task).

No exclusion criteria met (none). Inclusion criteria met: I1, I2, I3, I4. Inclusion criterion not demonstrated: regulation of emotional responses to visual stimuli as required by the meta-analysis objective — the study used idiographic sadness/guilt induction (autobiographical recall), not visual stimuli. Therefore excluded.

Abstract reports connectivity and treatment-response in major depression but does not describe a task-based emotion-regulation fMRI paradigm or task-related activation. Exclusion criteria: none met. Inclusion met: I3 (clinical participants). Inclusion not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation).

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study in humans (N=20) with task-related brain activation and healthy participants. It is unclear whether participants were instructed to regulate emotions (vs. passive viewing); therefore inclusion for full-text review is warranted to determine if the task meets the review's emotion-regulation criteria.

No explicit emotion-regulation instructions or strategy are described; the study examines anticipatory neural activity during speech anticipation but not a regulation task. Inclusion criteria met: I1, I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met/demonstrated: I2. Exclusion criteria met: none (E1/E2 not applicable).

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study in human participants performing an emotion regulation task (veterans with PTSD and controls), and reports task-related brain activation results (PFC, SMA changes). No exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review to extract detailed task contrasts and results.

Included for full-text review. Abstract reports a human (women with PTSD) neuroimaging study of emotional processing, but it does not specify whether a task-based emotion-regulation paradigm was used, whether task-related activation results are reported, or whether a control group is included. I1, I2, and I4 are not demonstrated in the abstract. No exclusion criteria are met based on the abstract.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion met: I3 (human clinical sample: youth with ADHD). Not met: I1 (not task-based; study examines intrinsic functional connectivity/resting-state), I2 (no emotion-regulation task reported), I4 (no task-related activation results reported). Therefore excluded from task-based emotion-regulation fMRI meta-analysis.

Excluded: PET meta-analysis of REM sleep, not a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation study. Inclusion met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion not met: I1 (not task-based fMRI), I2 (not an emotion regulation task), I4 (no task-related activation results reported). No exclusion criteria met.

EXCLUDED because the study investigates neural substrates of visual exploration/saccades, not emotion regulation. Exclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criteria not met: I2 (no emotion regulation task or instructions to amplify/dampen emotional responses).

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study using a cognitive reappraisal emotion regulation task in human participants and presents task-related brain activation results (vmPFC tracking of subjective and normative valence). No exclusion criteria are met.

Task-based fMRI in healthy adult humans reporting task-related brain activation (ACC). The abstract does not specify that participants were instructed to perform an emotion regulation strategy (uncertain whether anticipation counts as regulation), so I2 is not demonstrated from abstract alone; include for full-text review to resolve.

No exclusion criteria met. The study is a task-based fMRI study (I1), uses human participants (I3), and reports task-related brain activation results (I4). However participants viewed emotional scenes after a depletion manipulation and were not instructed to regulate their emotional responses; thus I2 (an emotion regulation task) is not demonstrated. Therefore exclude based on failure to meet I2.

Task-based fMRI study where participants regulated their own or another person's emotions (interpersonal emotion regulation). Healthy human sample (n=20) and report task-related brain activations. Does not meet exclusion criteria (not merely perspective-taking without regulation).

No exclusion criteria are met. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criteria not met/demonstrated: I2 (emotion regulation task) — abstract describes neural responses to negative facial stimuli but does not indicate participants were instructed to regulate their emotional responses, so it does not meet the emotion-regulation requirement.

E2 met: empathy study assessing spontaneous perception of others' pain without instructions to amplify/dampen emotional responses. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human ASD and control groups), I4 (task-related brain activations reported). Inclusion not met: I2 (no evidence of an emotion-regulation instruction/task).

Abstract reports a task-based whole-brain fMRI study with 55 healthy human participants performing instructed regulation of negative emotion (and viewing without regulating). Task-related activation results are reported (GLM contrasts and task-rest interactions). No exclusion criteria are met.

Task-based fMRI study using an affective face-processing task (likely passive viewing), with social anxiety disorder participants; reports task-related activation (left amygdala) and functional connectivity changes pre/post iCBT. The review accepts both emotion regulation and passive viewing paradigms, so inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Abstract reports task-based fMRI in human 4–6-year-old children examining functional brain activity related to emotion regulation. It is unclear whether participants were instructed to explicitly regulate emotions, so include for full-text review to confirm I2.

Excluded because abstract does not describe an emotion regulation task (I2 not met): the study examines decision-induced rationalization without instructions to regulate emotional responses. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related activations). No exclusion criteria met.

Task-based rtfMRI neurofeedback study in human combat veterans performing emotion regulation (positive autobiographical recall); reports task-related brain activation mediators and includes experimental and control groups. No exclusion criteria met.

Abstract does not specify a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation paradigm or report task-related brain activation results, but studies adults (human participants). Insufficient information to determine inclusion, so include for full-text review.

EXCLUDED because inclusion criterion I2 (emotion regulation task) is not met: study uses a Go/No-Go punishment/impulsivity paradigm, not an instructed emotion-regulation (e.g., reappraisal) task. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human healthy participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). No exclusion criteria (E1,E2) apply.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI RCT where patients viewed negative images or intentionally down-regulated affect using taught strategies, reports symptom change and normalization of brain activation—meeting all inclusion criteria and no exclusions evident.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (human clinical sample with control group). Inclusion criteria not met: I1 (study is resting-state, not task-based fMRI), I2 (no emotion regulation task performed), I4 (no task-related activation reported). Therefore excluded based on failure to meet task-based/emotion-regulation inclusion criteria.

Task-based fMRI study where participants with GAD performed explicit emotion regulation (acceptance, worry, suppression) and the abstract reports task-related brain activations and connectivity. Inclusion criteria met: I1, I2, I4. The abstract does not state whether a separate control group was included, so I3 is not demonstrated. No exclusion criteria met. Recommend full-text review to confirm sample/comparison details.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (healthy human participants), I4 (reports task-related connectivity/activation). Inclusion not met: I2 — study examines passive processing of emotional faces and genetic effects, not an emotion regulation instruction/strategy.

E2 met: study uses Theory-of-Mind/perspective-taking processing without instruction to amplify or dampen emotion. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human clinical and control groups). Inclusion not met/not demonstrated: I2 (no emotion-regulation task), I4 (reports connectivity rather than explicit task-related activation results).

Abstract reports task-based fMRI in human adolescents during an emotion regulation task (including passive viewing of negative vs neutral visual stimuli) and reports task-related vmPFC–amygdala functional connectivity linked to psychopathology, matching the review objective and inclusion criteria.

Task-based fMRI where participants ignored task-irrelevant unpleasant words (emotional interference), representing cognitive control of emotion/emotion regulation; includes non-patient groups (high AP/AR/AD and controls) and reports task-related functional connectivity results. All inclusion criteria I1–I4 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

Abstract describes task-based fMRI with human participants and task-related activations, but does not involve an emotion-regulation instruction or strategy (e.g., reappraisal/acceptance) nor explicit regulation of emotional responses to visual stimuli; therefore I2 not met. No exclusion criteria clearly apply.

E2: Study examines perception/evaluation of others (active listening) without instructions to amplify or dampen participants' own emotional responses (no emotion-regulation instruction). Inclusion met: I1, I3, I4. Inclusion not met: I2 (no evidence of an emotion-regulation task such as reappraisal or instructed modulation).

Task-based fMRI in adolescents/young adults reporting rVLPFC activation to negative emotional words and links to emotion reappraisal and alcohol use. The abstract does not clearly state whether participants were instructed to regulate emotion (versus passive viewing), so include for full-text review to confirm I2.

No evidence participants performed an emotion-regulation task (I2 not met). Abstract describes passive viewing and rating of aversive/neutral scenes; reports task fMRI activations (I1, I4) in clinical and control groups (I3). No exclusion criteria met.

Excluded because the study does not involve an emotion regulation task (I2 not met). It is a task-based fMRI study with healthy human participants and reports task-related activation (I1, I3, I4 met). No exclusion criteria apply.

Exclusion: none of the exclusion criteria apply. Inclusion met: I3 (human clinical sample with separate controls). Inclusion NOT met: I1 (not task-based; resting-state fMRI), I2 (no emotion-regulation task), I4 (no task-related activation results reported). Therefore exclude.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study where human participants used cognitive reappraisal to regulate cravings (personal-food images), and reports task-related neural activation (frontoparietal network, multivariate analyses). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a resting-state fMRI study of emotional intelligence, not a task-based emotion regulation study. Inclusion met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion not met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related activation results). No exclusion criteria met (E1,E2 not applicable).

E2 met: study examined empathy for others' pain (participants observed needles inserted into body parts) without any instruction to amplify or dampen their emotional response; thus it is not an emotion regulation task. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related activation). Inclusion not met: I2 (no evidence of an instructed emotion regulation task).

Abstract does not report whether this is a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation study or whether task-related activation contrasts meet inclusion criteria. Title suggests affect processing in methamphetamine dependence but provides insufficient detail. Include for full-text review to determine I1, I2, and I4.

Abstract reports human participants with social anxiety and neural/behavioral responses but does not specify that tasks were fMRI-based or involved explicit emotion regulation (or pure viewing), nor does it state task-related brain activation results. Key eligibility (I1, I2, I4) cannot be confirmed from abstract alone, so include for full-text review.

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human clinical and healthy control groups), I4 (task-related connectivity results). Inclusion not met: I2 — participants were engaged in an implicit facial-affect processing/viewing task with no instruction to regulate emotions, so an emotion-regulation task was not demonstrated.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study in humans (older adults) who performed an emotion-regulation task (increase/decrease responses to negative pictures, i.e., reappraisal/ regulation), and presents task-related brain activation results. No exclusion criteria are met in the abstract.

Task-based fMRI using an emotion-word Stroop with emotional distractors; examines cognitive control of emotion in presence of affective stimuli and reports task-related brain activation in human adults. Meets inclusion criteria for task-based fMRI, emotion regulation/cognitive control, human participants, and reported activation results.

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (task-related brain activation reported). Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I2 — not an emotion-regulation task and stimuli are auditory (infant laughter), whereas the meta-analysis targets regulation or passive viewing of visual stimuli. Thus study does not address the review objective.

Abstract provides insufficient information to determine whether this is a task-based fMRI study of emotion regulation. Title/summary mention empathy and neural/behavioural findings but do not state an emotion-regulation task or report task-related activation. No exclusion criteria are clearly met, so include for full-text review to assess I1–I4.

I2 not met: the task involves sadness introspection and judging nonemotional features, but participants were not instructed to regulate (e.g., reappraise, amplify, or dampen) their emotional responses. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human adolescent sample), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Exclusion met: none (E1 and E2 not applicable). Therefore exclude due to failure to meet I2 (emotion regulation task).

Abstract describes task-based fMRI in human participants and reports neural activity to emotional stimuli (I1, I3, I4 appear met). It does not specify that participants performed an emotion regulation task (I2 not demonstrated). Inclusion is uncertain from abstract alone, so include for full-text review.

Task-based fMRI study of implicit emotion processing (gender discrimination) in healthy human participants that reports task-related activation (amygdala BOLD response and functional connectivity) to emotional facial expressions. Although not an explicit regulation task, the meta-analysis includes passive viewing of emotional stimuli, so inclusion criterion for emotion-regulation/viewing is satisfied.

Task-based fMRI with human participants (OD/BPD and healthy controls) performing an oddball task requiring attention amid negative emotional distractors (interpretable as cognitive control of emotion/affective regulation), and reporting task-related activation differences. No exclusion criteria met.

Task-based fMRI study in humans performing an explicit emotion regulation task (maintain/enhance/suppress) with patient (mTBI) and control groups and reporting task-related brain activation, meeting I1,I2,I3,I4; no exclusions met.

E2 met: study is a mentalizing/Prisoner's Dilemma fMRI task without instruction to amplify or dampen participants' own emotional responses. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (healthy human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion not met: I2 (not an emotion-regulation task).

Abstract reports task-based fMRI in 9–19-year-olds and task-related amygdala activation (I1, I3, I4 met). However, it does not describe an emotion regulation instruction or strategy (no reappraisal, distancing, acceptance, or other regulation), so I2 is not demonstrated. No exclusion criteria (E1, E2) are met.

EXCLUDED: The task (Multi-Source Interference Task) is a cognitive interference/inhibition task, not an emotion-regulation or emotion-viewing task. Inclusion met: I1, I3, I4. Inclusion not met: I2 (no emotion-regulation instruction or emotional stimuli). Exclusion criteria met: none (E1/E2 not applicable).
